name: The Pentateuch (Torah): Law and Foundation

objectives.text: Name the five books of the Pentateuch in order
Retell the creation account in the order of the six days and the seventh day of rest
Retell the main events in the lives of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph
Identify Moses as the leader God called to bring Israel out of Egypt and to give them his law
Retell the Exodus account including the plagues, the Passover, and the crossing of the Red Sea
Recite the Ten Commandments in order
Explain that the Hebrew word Torah means instruction or law and that it names the first five books of the Bible
Describe the fall of Adam and Eve and the first promise of a Savior given in Genesis
Summarize the main content and storyline of each book of the Pentateuch
Explain the purpose of the tabernacle as the place where God chose to dwell among his people
Explain how the preface to the Ten Commandments shows that God gave his law to a people he had already redeemed
Compare the narrative sections of Genesis with the law sections of Leviticus in form and purpose
Describe the wilderness wanderings and explain from the text why Israel spent forty years in the desert
Explain the meaning of the Shema and its command to love God and teach his words to the next generation
Explain the covenant identity God gave Israel at Sinai as his treasured possession and a kingdom of priests
Trace the promises of land, offspring, and blessing given to Abraham through their partial fulfillment in the nation of Israel
Analyze the structure of Deuteronomy in light of ancient suzerain vassal treaties
Distinguish the moral, ceremonial, and judicial laws of the Pentateuch as the Reformed tradition classifies them
Interpret the holiness theme of Leviticus and explain how the New Testament applies it to God's people in Christ
Explain the purpose of the main offerings in the Levitical sacrificial system
Explain the rituals of the Day of Atonement and how Hebrews presents them as fulfilled in Christ
Analyze the Passover as a type that the New Testament applies to Jesus as the Lamb of God
Construct a timeline of the major events of the Pentateuch from creation to the death of Moses
Analyze how the generations formula organizes the book of Genesis
Explain how the Reformed tradition describes the continuing uses of the moral law summarized at Sinai
Evaluate the Documentary Hypothesis and the case for Mosaic authorship using internal biblical evidence
Evaluate arguments concerning the historical reliability of the patriarchal and Exodus narratives
Analyze how New Testament writers interpret the Pentateuch as pointing to Christ, including the promise of a prophet like Moses
Synthesize the Pentateuch's foundational teaching about God, humanity, and covenant into a coherent written account

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (five books, Ten Commandments, Torah meaning, tabernacle, genre comparison, Shema, treaty structure, holiness code, patriarchal promises, Day of Atonement, timeline, Documentary Hypothesis, synthesis). Merged Mosaic authorship into the Documentary Hypothesis evaluation and made historicity its own objective. Replaced 'Observe Creation and Exodus' with separate retelling objectives, and replaced 'Name Jesus as the Lamb of God' with a Passover typology analysis at grade 9. Moved Moses from 'main writer' at grade 1 to his role as leader and lawgiver. Added creation, patriarchs, the fall and first promise, book summaries, the preface to the law, wilderness wanderings, the Sinai covenant identity, the sacrificial system, the threefold division of the law, the uses of the law, the generations structure of Genesis, and New Testament use of the Pentateuch. Anchored each to specific verses and fitting Westminster and Heidelberg references.
